extracted.intended_audience: educators, teachers, educational theorists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Principles for how social environment and modes of direction (guidance vs control) function as the primary means of education; covers the school's roles in simplifying, purifying, and balancing experience and the nature of language, habit, and meaningful learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of language depends on shared activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of words arises from their use in shared activity; language ‘gains meaning in precisely the same way that the thing ... gains it, by being used in a given way.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the child learns 'hat' by watching and participating when the mother puts it on; learning about a 'Greek helmet' from words requires imaginative rehearsal of the activity in which it was used. When words are not tied to a shared or imaginative situation they act as mere physical stimuli (e.g., a foreign sound) rather than conveying meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning through participation and imaginative rehearsal
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding via language occurs because words incite the hearer/reader to 'rehearse imaginatively the activities in which the [object] has its use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical implication: teaching should engage learners in joint activity or prompt imaginative participation so terms become signs of shared action rather than abstract labels. Use concrete joint tasks, demonstrations, or guided imagery to connect words to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social environment forms dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Social environment 'forms the mental and emotional disposition of behavior in individuals by engaging them in activities that arouse and strengthen certain impulses, that have certain purposes and entail certain consequences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum and school design must account for habitual influences (language habits, manners, tastes). Example: a home of musicians will stimulate musical capacities. Recognize that many formative influences operate unconsciously and pervasively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education works indirectly by shaping environments
rubrics_metrics.description: 'We never educate directly, but indirectly by means of the environment.' Conscious teaching controls education only insofar as it deliberately regulates the environment's educative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designing environments (home, classroom, routines, materials) is the primary lever for shaping dispositions. Direct instruction alone cannot substitute for a thoughtfully organized social/physical environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: School function — simplify and order complex civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The school provides a 'simplified environment' by selecting fundamental features of civilization and establishing a progressive order so the young can assimilate complex social life 'piecemeal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should sequence material from simpler, more immediate uses toward more complex, abstract relations; avoid overwhelming learners with the full complexity of social life at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: School function — purify/select best elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The school 'eliminates ... the unworthy features of the existing environment' and 'by selecting the best for its exclusive use, it strives to reinforce the power of this best.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum choices should intentionally omit trivial or pernicious cultural elements and emphasize ideals that promote a better future society. Selection is an ethical and pedagogical act—decide which cultural practices to transmit.

rubrics_metrics.name: School function — balance and broaden social influences
rubrics_metrics.description: The school should 'balance the various elements in the social environment' so individuals can 'escape from the limitations of the social group in which he was born' and encounter a broader, more balanced environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster mixing of different races, religions, customs, and backgrounds through common subject matter and shared activities to create a unity of outlook and counteract centrifugal social forces. Aim for inclusive, common experiences that broaden perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: School as integrator of competing social codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The school 'coordinates within the disposition of each individual the diverse influences of the various social environments ...' providing a 'steadying and integrating office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students to reconcile conflicting standards encountered in family, work, religion, and public life by providing a consistent set of norms and integrative experiences across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferring guidance/direction over coercive control
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes direction, control, and guidance: guidance 'assists through cooperation the natural capacities'; control often connotes coercion. Education should avoid misconceiving control as sheer external compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor methods that enlist the learner's participation and existing tendencies rather than imposing outcomes by force. Recognize that seemingly coercive measures may produce compliance without moral or educative change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction requires focusing and ordering (simultaneous and successive aspects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction is both 'focusing and ordering': spatially selecting tendencies to center energy on the point of need, and temporally arranging successive acts so each helps what follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design lessons and tasks that both concentrate effort on relevant skills (focus) and sequence activities so earlier acts scaffold later development (order). Use progressive exercises that prepare learners for subsequent stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: External stimuli cannot create responses without existing tendencies
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Purely external direction is impossible. The environment can at most only supply stimuli to call out responses. These responses proceed from tendencies already possessed by the individual.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before attempting to direct behavior, assess learners' existing instincts, habits, and knowledge. Effective re-direction builds on what is already present; ignore that and efforts will likely fail or backfire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflating physical compliance with educative change
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical results (e.g., enforced confinement, forced actions) may not alter disposition or understanding: 'A man can be prevented ... by shutting him up, but shutting him up may not alter his disposition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disciplinary measures judiciously; prioritize approaches that foster understanding, internal motives, and moral judgment rather than mere obedience. Seek evidence of internalization, not just outward compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit conscious coercive methods; rely on ambient social direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscious methods (punishment, shame, rebuke, appeal to approbation) are obvious but should be limited; the 'more important and permanent mode of control' is the everyday use of things and practices by those around the immature person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize modelling, immersion in productive routines, and structuring the student's day-to-day activities. Make desirable behaviors the natural, habitual practices of the community rather than only enforcing them by sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning arises from use of things, not mere sensory impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrasts false psychology (learning by aggregate sensations) with the view that 'it is the characteristic use to which the thing is put ... which supplies the meaning with which it is identified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach through purposeful use of tools and objects in real tasks (chairs for sitting, oranges for eating), not by presenting isolated sensory properties. Contextualize objects in their functions and social uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform blind habit into intelligent, purposive response
rubrics_metrics.description: Habits formed by repeated blind responses 'possess us' unless we become aware and 'pass judgment upon the worth of the result.' Education turns automatic responses into acts performed 'for the sake of its meaning.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reflection on habits and the consequences of actions. Create opportunities for learners to understand why they act as they do and to choose or revise habits based on judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared activity requires common understanding, not mere juxtaposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes between mere simultaneous contribution to a result and genuine conjoint activity: true shared activity occurs only when each participant 'views the consequences of his own acts as having a bearing upon what others are doing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design cooperative tasks that require mutual awareness of goals and interdependence (not assembly-line-style disconnected tasks). Assess whether participants understand the common intent and consequences of their roles; if not, restructure the activity so meaning and mutual responsiveness are explicit.
